sections.h2: Where do I take a deed to be recorded in Shelby County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Take it to the Shelby County Recorder on the second floor of the county annex at 129 E. Court Street in Sidney. Phone 937-498-7270 or fax 937-498-7272 to reach staff. The counter takes new recordings a quarter hour before the staff stops other business: Monday to Thursday that means a 4:15 p.m. cutoff against a 4:30 p.m. close, and on Fridays 11:45 a.m. against noon. Plan to arrive well ahead of those times.

The Recorder's page calls the office the steward of the county's real estate records and says they reach back to the county's start, when the land was still part of Miami County. The online index covers July 1, 1989 forward. Older research means a trip to the office, and staff will help, though they do not do genealogy searches for outsiders.

Sidney is the only city in the county, and the rest of Shelby County is villages, townships and farmland. A deed here may describe a Sidney street lot, a village house in a place with German roots, or acreage along the Great Miami River.

sections.h2: What does Shelby County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Under the county's 2025 schedule, a deed costs $39 for its first two pages, with $8 for every added page. The schedule explains that most recording fees climbed $5 on January 1, 2025, after Senate Bill 94 added a document preservation surcharge, which ORC 317.32 limits to five dollars.

Shelby County Recorder charges on the 2025 schedule
ServiceCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease and most filings$39 covers the first two pages
Each added page or attachment$8
Marginal notation$4 each
Non-standardization fee, per document$20
Plat, 11 by 17 inches$40
Plat, 24 by 36 inches$86
UCC financing statement$12 plus $4 per name indexed

Count the pages before you write the check, because the total moves with each added sheet and each attachment.

sections.h2: What do Shelby County recorder staff look for in a deed?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee page lists the rules plainly:

  • Every document needs a legal description, and it must read as it does on the prior deed. A description with missing parts is rejected.
  • Mail filings need a self-addressed stamped envelope. Without postage for the return, the office holds the document.
  • Marginal notations require the volume and page of the earlier record, and each one adds $4.
  • An affidavit has to say who the current owner of the property is.

The grantor's signature must be acknowledged by an authorized officer, usually a notary, under ORC 5301.01. An unacknowledged deed is not ready for the counter.

The county page also posts a public notice on old deed language. Any clause that limits the sale, rental or use of a dwelling by race, color, sex, religion, national origin, handicap or familial status is invalid under federal fair housing law and cannot be enforced, even if it sits in a decades-old recorded deed.

sections.h2: Who collects the Shelby County conveyance fee?
sections.html:
The Shelby County Auditor does, before the Recorder files anything. The Auditor's transfer fee page prints the real estate transfer fee as $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus $.50 per parcel.

The rate rests on ORC 319.54(G)(3) and the county option in ORC 322.02. The county option falls on the grantor, which makes the seller the usual payer when the deed is delivered.

A few transfers are listed as exempt, among them family gifts, corrective deeds and deeds where no money changes hands. Ask the Auditor before assuming a deal qualifies.

sections.h2: What is the land like in Shelby County?
sections.html:
Shelby County sits in western Ohio and covers 411 square miles, with 408 of them land. Wikipedia describes low rolling hills, almost all of it farmed or built up. The Great Miami River enters from Logan County near the middle and leaves into Miami County. The highest ground, 1,149 feet, lies in the southeast corner where Champaign and Miami counties meet it.

The 2020 census counted 48,230 residents, with about 43 percent in urban areas and a median age of 40.2. The county is named for Isaac Shelby, Kentucky's first governor, and borders Auglaize, Logan, Champaign, Miami, Darke and Mercer counties, so a parcel near the line can sit close to a neighboring recorder's records. The county's first seat of government was Hardin, named for a pioneer killed there in 1792, before Sidney took over. When the county was cut down in 1848, Minster and New Bremen moved into the new Auglaize County. Many Shelby County towns trace to German immigrants, and the Miami and Erie Canal, which reached the county in 1841, gave those newcomers early work.

For a seller, the geography means plenty of rural parcels. A farmhouse on a few acres may need a survey or a split approved before it can be deeded separately, so ask the Auditor's office early about description rules.

sections.h2: What is the order of steps from signing to a recorded Shelby County deed?
sections.html:
There are four steps, in this order. The grantor signs before a notary. The deed goes to the Shelby County Auditor with the transfer fee, which the Auditor's page prices at $4 per $1,000 of price plus $.50 per parcel. The deed then goes to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a stamped return envelope if it travels by mail. Last, the Recorder indexes it, and the new owner's name appears in the county's records.

A title company normally carries a deed through those steps at a closing. A family member handling a transfer alone can do the same in person or by mail. Both offices are county offices in Sidney, so ask each for its current hours before you go, and remember that the Recorder stops taking recordings 15 minutes before it closes.

Once the filing posts, the online index from July 1, 1989 forward lets anyone confirm it, so a seller can confirm the deed went on record.

sections.h2: How do Shelby County property tax records and relief programs work?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate section covers valuation and tax rates, revaluation information, owner occupancy and homestead tax reductions, delinquent payment plans and razed or damaged structures. A seller can search a parcel there to see the value on record before listing.

  • A value dispute begins as a Board of Revision complaint. ORC 5715.19 allows filing with the auditor until March 31 of the next year, or until the first-half collection closes if that falls later.
  • The Ohio Department of Taxation lists the 2026 homestead reduction for seniors and disabled owners at $29,700 of value, with the application filed in the same year by December 31.
  • Back taxes can sometimes be paid through a delinquent payment plan, which the Auditor's menu lists. Ask there for terms.

At closing the title agent requests the tax payoff from the county. Because Ohio bills real estate in two halves, the amount owed depends on when in the year the sale closes.

faqs.q: What are the Shelby County Recorder's hours for recording a deed?
faqs.a: New recordings are accepted until 4:15 p.m. Monday to Thursday and until 11:45 a.m. Friday. Other office business continues 15 minutes longer each day, per the Recorder's page.

faqs.q: How much is the Shelby County recording fee for a two-page deed?
faqs.a: $39 on the 2025 schedule, which covers the first two pages. Pages beyond that cost $8 each, a non-standard document adds $20, and each marginal notation adds $4.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder hold my deed if I mail it?
faqs.a: Yes, if you leave out the return envelope. The county asks that mailed documents come with a stamped, self-addressed envelope, and without one the office holds the paper instead of mailing it back.

faqs.q: What is the Shelby County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor's page prints the real estate transfer fee as $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus fifty cents for each parcel. It is paid at the Auditor's office, ahead of recording.

faqs.q: Can I search Shelby County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Partly. The Recorder's website carries an index from July 1, 1989 forward. Earlier books stay at the office, where staff help visitors search but do not take genealogy requests.
